data.value: Save or discard the keymap edit to change the keyboard.

data.name: Settings_BackgroundOpacityHint
data.value: How solid the dark fill behind the keyboard is — drop to 0 for a fully transparent overlay.

data.name: Settings_PressHighlightHint
data.value: Color of the dot that pops on each pressed key.

data.name: Settings_ColorTrayIcon
data.value: Color tray icon by active layer

data.name: Settings_ColorTrayIconHint
data.value: Tint the system tray icon with the active layer's color so you can read the layer at a glance when the window is hidden. Turn off if it clashes with your menu bar.

data.name: Settings_GlobalHotkeyHint
data.value: Press this key from anywhere to toggle the layer overlay. Whichever key you pick is excluded from the layer-key list below.

data.name: Settings_MouseLayer_Hint
data.value: While the mouse is moving, push the chosen layer to the keyboard. When the mouse stays idle for the timeout below, revert. Requires the keyboard to be connected over Raw HID.

data.name: Settings_MouseLayer_EndlessTimeout
data.value: Endless timeout (only exit via the options below)

data.name: Settings_MouseLayer_EndlessTimeout_Hint
data.value: When checked, the idle timeout is disabled and the mouse layer stays pushed until a transparent or empty key is pressed. At least one of the options below must remain enabled.

data.name: Settings_MouseLayer_ExitOnTransparent_Hint
data.value: While the mouse layer is pushed, pressing a key whose binding on the active layer matches an enabled option above reverts immediately. Move the mouse again to re-arm.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_Hint
data.value: Rules are evaluated in order; the first whose match text is a case-insensitive substring of the focused app's process name wins. Editing rules persists immediately. When enabled, the matched layer is pushed to the keyboard on every focus change.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_Enable
data.value: Enable auto-switch (push matched layer to keyboard on focus change)

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_FallbackLabel
data.value: When focus moves to an app with no rule:

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_ExitKeysHint
data.value: Pick one key on the keyboard. Double-tapping it while a rule layer is active falls back to the selected layer above; double-tapping again returns to the rule's layer. Best picked on a key whose binding emits no OS keystrokes.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_ExitOnTransparent_Hint
data.value: While a rule layer is active, pressing a key whose binding on that layer matches an enabled option above falls back immediately. Double-tap the exit key to re-enter the rule.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_PickExitKeysHint
data.value: Tap one key to set the auto-switch exit key. Tap the selected key to remove it. The chosen key will fire on a double-tap.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_PickExitKeysCandidates
data.value: Good candidates: keys that emit no OS keystroke (e.g. a bare modifier like Shift/Ctrl, or any key bound to &none) — that way double-tapping doesn't leak characters into the focused app.

data.name: Settings_AutoSwitch_Empty
data.value: No rules yet. Add one above.

data.name: Settings_LayersHint
data.value: Choose which layer buttons appear on the layer bar and customize each layer's color. Hidden layers still show when the keyboard switches to them.

data.name: Settings_LayerShowTooltip
data.value: Show this layer's button on the layer bar

data.name: Settings_CliTool_Hint
data.value: Install the 'lviz' command so scripts can drive LViz (e.g. lviz event ci:ok).

data.name: Settings_AutoCheckHint
data.value: When enabled, LViz checks for a new release shortly after launch and notifies you in this panel.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_Hint
data.value: A pipeline is a named list of steps run in order: push a keyboard layer, set a device's RGB or pointing options, launch an app or shell command, or wait. Bind a pipeline to a signal a key fires to run it from the keyboard.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_Empty
data.value: No pipelines yet. Add one above, then add steps to it.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_NoSelection
data.value: Select a pipeline to edit its steps.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_BindingsHint
data.value: Map a signal id a key fires (signal.fire) to a pipeline. The id is opaque on the wire — its meaning lives here.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_EventBindingsHint
data.value: Map a host event id a script fires (lviz event <id>) to a pipeline. The id is an opaque string — its meaning lives here.

data.name: Settings_Pipeline_AppLayerBindingsHint
data.value: Run a pipeline when an auto-switch rule enters, leaves, exits, or re-enters its layer. Triggers come from your auto-switch rules (set those up first); the pipeline runs alongside the layer change, not instead of it. One pipeline per trigger.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_Hint
data.value: Forward an action one device emits (e.g. a key bound to “set DPI”) to whatever other device handles it. The keyboard and the handler never talk directly — LViz brokers between them. Discovery runs whenever the keyboard is connected; this switch only controls forwarding.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_Available
data.value: Routing available — a trigger has a matching handler on another device.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_ControlReady
data.value: A compatible device is connected — send actions to it under “Send action to device” below. Connect a second device where one triggers what the other handles to route between them.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_NoProtocol
data.value: No connected device speaks the capability protocol yet.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_NoRoutes
data.value: No routes — a device must trigger a capability another device handles.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_ControlHint
data.value: Advanced: have LViz originate an action itself, instead of forwarding one. Handy for testing a handler device.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_ControlPickTarget
data.value: Pick a target device above to see the actions it accepts.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_ControlNone
data.value: This device exposes no actions LViz can send directly.

data.name: Settings_DeviceRouting_ControlGone
data.value: That device is no longer connected.
